category: managed NoSQL document database with key-value, SQL++, search and vector workloads

free_tier.stated: One free tier operational cluster per organization: 1 node, 8 GB RAM, 8 to 10 GB data storage depending on cloud, SQL++ and key value, Search (vector, FTS, geo), Mobile App Services, RBAC with scopes and collections, forum support; no credit card required and free for continuous use while active
free_tier.notes: The pricing page states 1 node and 8 GB of RAM. Cloud reference pages give the data-storage allowance as 10 GB on AWS and Azure and 8 GB on GCP. The plan is perpetual while the cluster is active, not a trial.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: the free-tier page does not state a per-document size cap; the Capella Data API platform limit is 100 MB per request and response payload, but that is an interface limit and not a stated per-object cap on the free tier
per_object_cap.notes: The 100 MB figure is the Data API payload limit and is recorded under limits[] as an interface cap, not as a per-object cap.

retention.stated: Data and state are preserved while the cluster is active. After more than 72 hours without activity Couchbase turns off the free cluster and linked App Services, preserving data and state; after more than 30 days without activity Couchbase deletes the cluster and linked App Services. Upgrading from the free plan to a paid Support plan also deletes the existing free cluster.
retention.notes: days is the inactivity period that triggers deletion. The 72-hour mark only turns the cluster off and preserves data; the 30-day mark deletes it.

egress.terms: Capella passes through cloud-provider data transfer charges based on GiB and transfer type. Internet egress is commonly .09 credits per GB in North American and European regions; inter-zone or intra-region transfer is commonly .01 credit per GB on AWS and GCP and free on Azure. Data import into Capella and transfer between instances in the same Availability Zone are free. No free egress allowance is published for the free plan.

interface_detail: Couchbase SDKs (Java, Python, Node.js, PHP and others) connect over the couchbases:// TLS protocol; a RESTful Data API exposes document CRUD under /v1/ with passthrough to Query and Search services; a Management API and the Capella web console manage the cluster.
tooling: Couchbase SDKs (Java, Python, Node.js, PHP), any HTTP client such as curl or Postman against the Data API, the cbbackupmgr CLI for backup, the Capella web console, and a Management API key for automation
chaining: A free Capella cluster can hold a document and vector store behind a free Worker or tunnel for a public REST path, with the SDK or Data API as the write interface.

limits.value: 1 free tier operational cluster per organization; 10 GB data storage on AWS and Azure and 8 GB on GCP; 1 node, 8 GB RAM
cluster turns off after more than 72 hours of inactivity with data preserved, and is deleted after more than 30 days of inactivity
Data API is limited to 10,000 requests per second per node; payloads restricted to 100 MB

binding_note: The cluster is deleted after 30 days without activity, so a workload with a persistent idle gap fails before the 8 to 10 GB storage or the 10,000 requests per second interface limit is reached.

identity_cost.detail: The sign-up page offers Email Address, GitHub Account or Google Account. Email signup asks for Full Name, Email Address and a password of at least 12 characters, then an email confirmation code and agreement to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. The billing docs state no credit balance or credit card is needed for the Free plan.

reliability_note: The free cluster turns off after 72 hours idle and is deleted after 30 days idle; upgrading to a paid plan deletes the existing free cluster, and the backup and restore, private endpoint, network peering, audit log and on/off schedule features are not available on the free tier.
confidence_note: All figures come from first-party Couchbase pricing, product, billing and docs pages captured and quoted on 2026-11-19. No probe was run, so the rung stays documented.

evidence.quote: The Capella free tier offers a fully managed NoSQL DBaaS with credits, sample data, SQL++ queries, search, mobile sync, and a small cluster (≈1 node, ~8GB) for prototyping – no credit card required.

notes: The free tier is a real managed Couchbase Server cluster, not a sandbox. Two caveats bind: the cluster is deleted after 30 days idle and upgrading to a paid plan deletes it, so data must be backed out with cbbackupmgr before either. The storage allowance differs by cloud: 10 GB on AWS and Azure, 8 GB on GCP. The per-document cap is not published; the 100 MB figure is the Data API payload limit, not a free-tier object cap. Couchbase Server is also available as self-hosted software, but that offer is the last resort and is not the offer recorded here.
